description: Shrink a video file by re-encoding it at a lower bitrate. Pick Low, Medium or High quality and compare the original and new file sizes.

faqs.a: Low targets about 0.5 Mbps (max 640 px wide), Medium about 1.5 Mbps (max 1280 px) and High about 3 Mbps (up to 1920 px). Output is WebM, or MP4 on Safari.
faqs.q: What do the quality settings mean?

faqs.a: Re-encoding always involves some quality trade-off, but Medium and High stay visually close to the original for most footage.
faqs.q: Will the compressed video look much worse?

faqs.a: Yes — the video is re-encoded locally on your device and never uploaded anywhere.

howto: Choose a video file from your device.
Pick a quality level: Low, Medium or High.
Click "Compress Video" and wait while it is re-encoded.
Compare the original and compressed sizes, then download the smaller file.
title: Video Compressor
